reference: Independent contract rows derive from synthetic sysfs attributes, documented 512-byte sectors, and encoded ext2 magic. GNU util-linux lsblk cannot consume this private sysfs tree without a reviewed path adapter; no GNU enumeration parity is claimed.
coverage: Synthetic disk/partition NAME, MAJ:MIN, RM, SIZE, RO, and TYPE output
Pairs output, ASCII tree shape, flat nodeps listing, and disk operand filtering
exclusions: No live /sys or /dev inventory is read; real-device enumeration is deferred.
GNU lsblk could not serve as a sysfs oracle in this sandbox because its --sysroot option did not redirect /sys access.
GPT labels, mountpoint lookup, statvfs-derived usage, and live filesystem probing are not covered.
No actual device is created, attached, opened for mutation, or otherwise changed.

cases.purpose: Bash reports lsblk as a builtin, and its help contains the documented sysfs scope and exit-code section.
cases.script:
type_text=$(type -t lsblk)
help_text=$(help lsblk)
[[ $type_text == builtin ]]
[[ $help_text == *"Walks /sys/class/block."* ]]
[[ $help_text == *"Exit codes:"* ]]
printf '%s\n' "$type_text"

cases.purpose: A fixture with one disk and two partitions has independently encoded pairs rows for major:minor, removable/read-only flags, 512-byte-sector size, and type.
cases.script:
root=fixture
mkdir -p \
  "$root/sys/class/block" "$root/sys/dev/block" \
  "$root/sys/devices/virtual/block/vda/vda1" \
  "$root/sys/devices/virtual/block/vda/vda2" \
  "$root/dev" "$root/proc"
ln -s class/block "$root/sys/block"
ln -s ../../devices/virtual/block/vda "$root/sys/class/block/vda"
ln -s ../../devices/virtual/block/vda/vda1 "$root/sys/class/block/vda1"
ln -s ../../devices/virtual/block/vda/vda2 "$root/sys/class/block/vda2"
ln -s ../../class/block/vda "$root/sys/dev/block/8:0"
ln -s ../../class/block/vda1 "$root/sys/dev/block/8:1"
ln -s ../../class/block/vda2 "$root/sys/dev/block/8:2"
write_attrs() {
  local base=$1 majmin=$2 sectors=$3 removable=$4 readonly=$5 partno=$6
  printf '%s\n' "$majmin" > "$base/dev"
  printf '%s\n' "$sectors" > "$base/size"
  printf '%s\n' "$removable" > "$base/removable"
  printf '%s\n' "$readonly" > "$base/ro"
  if [[ -n $partno ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$partno" > "$base/partition"
  fi
}
write_attrs "$root/sys/devices/virtual/block/vda" 8:0 1 1 0 ''
write_attrs "$root/sys/devices/virtual/block/vda/vda1" 8:1 1 0 1 1
write_attrs "$root/sys/devices/virtual/block/vda/vda2" 8:2 1 0 0 2
: > "$root/proc/mounts"
run_lsblk() {
  BASHLSBLK_SYS_BLOCK_DIR="$root/sys/class/block" \
  BASHLSBLK_DEV_ROOT="$root/dev" \
  BASHLSBLK_PROC_MOUNTS="$root/proc/mounts" \
    lsblk "$@"
}
run_lsblk --pairs --noheadings --output NAME,MAJ:MIN,RM,SIZE,RO,TYPE
cases.stdout:
NAME="vda" MAJ:MIN="8:0" RM="1" SIZE="512B" RO="0" TYPE="disk"
NAME="vda1" MAJ:MIN="8:1" RM="0" SIZE="512B" RO="1" TYPE="part"
NAME="vda2" MAJ:MIN="8:2" RM="0" SIZE="512B" RO="0" TYPE="part"

cases.purpose: Check enumeration and topology for actual kernel block devices, including loop or device-mapper nodes, without touching or changing them.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with explicitly provisioned virtual block devices and a known sysfs inventory, or a separately reviewed sysfs/device mock. The shared host inventory and real device nodes are out of scope.

cases.purpose: Compare the synthetic block tree directly against GNU util-linux lsblk once the reference can consume the same sysfs fixture.
cases.reason: The mandatory controller sandbox has no /sys/dev/block, and GNU lsblk --sysroot does not redirect that sysfs lookup. Requires a future isolated reference mode with a disposable /sys mock or an independently validated GNU lsblk build that accepts a sysfs root.
